transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-26
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sara Voss (Quantum Atelier CTO), Miguel Alvarez (Lead ML Eng), Priya Kothari (Security), Ben (Product PM)

Summary:
Sara is evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing assistant across EU and NA customers. Primary concerns: time-to-first-token for a PLG flow, data residency/SOC2, and whether to start on Hosted API or go straight to Dedicated/Private. They want an actionable quickstart pathway and a short benchmark to inform cost vs latency tradeoffs.

Topics:
- Quickstart / free credits / TTFT (time-to-first-token)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
- Performance: latency SLOs, batching, KV cache, quantization
- Next steps and pilot scope

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Liam my SE is here as well. How's everyone doing?
00:06 Sara Voss: Hi Maya, hi Liam. Good thanks. We set aside an hour, so appreciate it.
00:12 Miguel Alvarez: Hey all. Quick note — we've got half the infra folks on standby in case we dive deep.
00:18 Maya Chen: Great. Agenda is quick: understand your constraints, walk through TTFT and quickstart, then high level hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs, and close with next steps. Sound good?
00:25 Ben (Product PM): Yep.
00:28 Priya Kothari: Works for me.
00:34 Liam O'Connor: I'll jump in on the perf and infra bits. To start, can you give us a quick sense of the workload? Expected QPS, typical prompt lengths, and any PII/residency needs?
00:45 Sara Voss: Sure. We're building a contextual assistant for our enterprise customers. Initial traffic target is small — maybe 5 to 10 rps for pilot, spike to 50 rps over time. Typical prompts are 200 to 400 tokens, but we do some multi-turn state so KV cache is relevant.
01:01 Miguel Alvarez: Also sensitive: EU customer data must stay in EU region; some redaction applied on our side but retention rules apply.
01:09 Maya Chen: Got it. So TTFT — most customers who want a PLG path want to see a very fast path from sign-up to first call. Our quickstart typically gets devs to first successful API call in under 30 minutes. We provide free credits — I'll grant a 100k token pack which usually covers a decent first-run.
01:25 Sara Voss: Is that free credits per account or do you do per-org entitlements? We have multiple product teams.
01:32 Maya Chen: It's per account; we can set up multiple sub-accounts or invite users. For enterprise pilots we also do larger credit grants — we can tailor.
01:40 Miguel Alvarez: On the EU requirement: if we start Hosted, can you guarantee data residency? Or do we need Private from the start?
01:48 Liam O'Connor: We host in multiple regions. For the Hosted API we can pin requests to EU region endpoints which keep data in EU datacenters. That said, for strict regulatory customers Private (VPC) or Dedicated with contractual data isolation is the recommended path. Also SOC2 reports and DPA clauses apply — Maya can share the compliance pack.
02:11 Priya Kothari: Worth calling out — we need KMS integration and HSM options for key management.
02:17 Liam O'Connor: Yep, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys. For Dedicated we have options for bring-your-own-keys with a contractual commitment. Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default but we do envelope encryption and strong controls.
02:33 Ben: On the perf side — we care about latency tail. If a user interacts with the assistant, we want sub-400ms token latency for short prompts. Is that realistic on hosted?
02:43 Liam O'Connor: Sub-400ms per token depends a lot on model choice and batching. For smaller models and optimized kernels you can get pretty low latency. For more deterministic latency we recommend Dedicated with pinned capacity. We also have smart routing that can fall back to smaller quantized variants under load.
02:58 Miguel Alvarez: Can you explain the KV cache mention? We heard that Redwood caches prefixes to speed multi-turn.
03:05 Liam O'Connor: Yes — we do prefix caching and KV cache to avoid re-computing long contexts. That gives a pretty big perf boost for multi-turn flows. It also interacts with billing — if you keep sessions warm we can amortize cost.
03:20 Sara Voss: For the quickstart, what's the actual path we'd follow? We want product folks to try the API without involving infra for a week.
03:28 Maya Chen: Typical flow: 1) sign up self-serve, 2) apply credits (I'll seed the account), 3) follow a quickstart repo (curl/SDK examples) to make first generate and embeddings calls. We provide a sample prompt set and a notebook for a simple assistant. Most teams hit first token within 15–30 minutes.
03:43 Ben: And SDKs — do you have Node/Python and also a local emulator or CLI?
03:48 Maya Chen: Node, Python, Go SDKs and a CLI. The docs include a Postman collection as well.
03:53 Priya Kothari: On compliance — can you share SOC 2 and your pen test cadence? Also audit logs retention?
04:00 Maya Chen: Absolutely. I'll share our SOC 2 Type II report, pen-test summary, and details about audit log retention. For Private we can offer longer retention and integrations with SIEMs.
04:14 Miguel Alvarez: If we start with Hosted, can we later migrate to Dedicated without code changes?
04:20 Liam O'Connor: That's by design — same API surface. You can pin model versions and rollout policies independently. Migration is primarily a config change and potentially switching endpoints if you're using a VPC. We help with migration scripts.
04:33 Sara Voss: Okay that's helpful. Cost — any rule of thumb for per-token costs vs self-hosted?
04:38 Liam O'Connor: Hosted is usage-based and competitive; Dedicated is a reserved capacity model — you trade predictability for lower unit cost at scale. Self-hosting usually has higher ops overhead; we can run a cost model for your expected load to show TCO.
04:52 Ben: Could you do a short benchmark comparing responses for our typical prompt (we can share representative prompts) so we can make the hosted vs dedicated decision?
04:59 Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. If you share a small set of prompts and endpoints, we'll run a latency and cost-per-token run across a couple model variants and include batching/quantization settings.
05:12 Sara Voss: Great. What's the minimum time to run that? We want results before our architecture review next week.
05:17 Liam O'Connor: We can deliver a bench within a week if we get prompts and a test dataset today — small dataset. Plan for 5 business days.
05:25 Miguel Alvarez: Acceptable. A few more detailed questions — network egress: for Hosted, does data flow outside our VPC? How do you secure traffic?
05:33 Liam O'Connor: Hosted API is a managed endpoint. For strict network controls you want Private with VPC peering or on-prem. We use TLS everywhere, mTLS options for dedicated/private, and support IP allowlists.
05:47 Priya Kothari: Do you have SSO options? We standardize on SAML and Okta.
05:51 Maya Chen: Yes SSO with SAML/Okta and OIDC is supported. We also have RBAC at the token level.
05:58 Ben: One risk flag from our side: vendors that change model outputs between versions. Do you support pinned model versions and guardrails?
06:06 Liam O'Connor: Yes, you can pin model versions in the config and we have rollout policies (canary, A/B) and automatic fallback to earlier models if regressions are detected. We also integrate with evals so you can run prompt-based quality checks post-deploy.
06:20 Sara Voss: There were some notes in the doc about quantization — if we use quantized models does output quality drop?
06:27 Liam O'Connor: There's a small tradeoff depending on model/quantization approach. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations for when quantization is appropriate by workload; we'll include model-specific diffs in the bench.
06:38 Miguel Alvarez: Ok — operationally, who would we loop in for a pilot? We'll need infra (for VPC/net), security for the DPA, and product to run the prompts.
06:47 Sara Voss: I'll coordinate internal owners.
06:50 Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick friction items to resolve: 1) I'll seed credits and quickstart, 2) Liam will run a perf bench if you share prompts, 3) Priya will share compliance matrix and residency constraints. Any timeline notes?
07:03 Priya Kothari: We need the compliance docs by Friday so we can feed legal.
07:08 Maya Chen: I'll send the SOC2 & security pack by EOD tomorrow.
07:12 Miguel Alvarez: And bench by 11/02 is good.
07:15 Ben: One more question — will we get access to token-level cost reporting during trial?
07:20 Maya Chen: Yes, console access includes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route. We'll include a short guide on using the console.
07:28 Sara Voss: Sounds good. Any gotchas we should be aware of launching quickstart internally?
07:33 Liam O'Connor: Make sure to set a reasonable prompt length limit and enable KV cache for multi-turn tests, and be mindful of burst rate — we'll show a sample autoscaling config if you move to Dedicated.
07:46 (crosstalk) Speaker 2: sorry to interrupt — how does billing handle cached tokens vs new tokens?
07:53 Maya Chen: Good question, caching affects compute but billing counts generated tokens; prompt tokens are accounted for, but we have prefix caching considerations. We'll add a short note in the cost explainer.
08:07 Sara Voss: Great. If we decide to go Private later, what's the procurement lead time?
08:12 Maya Chen: Private/on-prem can be 6–10 weeks depending on contract and infra setup; Dedicated is usually 2–4 weeks after PO. Hosted is immediate.
08:23 Ben: That helps.
08:26 Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps: I'll seed 100k tokens and share quickstart + SOC2/security pack by tomorrow. Liam will draft a bench plan; we expect results by 2026-11-02. Priya will drop the compliance matrix.
08:41 Sara Voss: Thanks. We'll share prompts today and loop infra.
08:45 Miguel Alvarez: Noted.
08:47 Maya Chen: Anything else?
08:50 Sara Voss: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
08:53 Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with meeting notes and action items.
